title: The edge-connectivity threshold for positive Lin–Lu–Yau curvature is not $\lceil 2n/3 - 1 \rceil$ for all $n \ge 3$
abstract: For each integer $n \ge 3$, let $c(n)$ be the smallest integer $k$ such that every connected simple graph on $n$ vertices with edge-connectivity at least $k$ has strictly positive Lin–Lu–Yau curvature on every edge. A question asked in arXiv:2610.10559 is whether $c(n) = \lceil 2n/3 - 1 \rceil$ for all $n \ge 3$. This question is answered in the negative. The conjectured formula fails at $n = 3$, where every connected graph on 3 vertices has positive Lin–Lu–Yau curvature on every edge, yielding $c(3) = 0$ while the formula evaluates to $1$. Furthermore, the failure is not limited to this degenerate case: an exact computation shows that $c(5) = 2$ whereas $\lceil 2 \cdot 5 / 3 - 1 \rceil = 3$. The refutation has been formalized and verified in Lean.
introduction:
For each integer $n \ge 3$, let $c(n)$ denote the smallest integer $k$ such that every connected simple graph $G$ on $n$ vertices with edge-connectivity $\kappa'(G) \ge k$ satisfies $\kappa_{\mathrm{LLY}}(x, y) > 0$ for all edges $xy \in E(G)$.

In arXiv:2610.10559, Theorem 1.3 proves that an edge-connectivity of at least $2n/3 - 1$ guarantees $\kappa_{\mathrm{LLY}}(x, y) > 0$ for every edge. Furthermore, Theorem 1.4 of arXiv:2610.10559 establishes sharpness of this bound by constructing counterexample graphs with edge-connectivity $\kappa'(G) = 2n/3 - 2$ and an edge of negative curvature, under the hypothesis that $2n/3$ is an even integer at least $6$. Following Theorem 1.4, arXiv:2610.10559 asked whether $c(n) = \lceil 2n/3 - 1 \rceil$ for all $n \ge 3$, leaving open the exact threshold for general values of $n$, particularly when $2n/3$ is not an even integer.

This post presents a Lean 4 formalization refuting this question. Specifically, the theorem `not_forall_lly_positive_edge_connectivity_threshold_eq_ceil` shows that the proposed formula fails at $n = 3$, where $c(3) = 0$ while $\lceil 2 \cdot 3 / 3 - 1 \rceil = 1$. The formalization also includes the non-degenerate failure at $n = 5$, where $c(5) = 2$ while $\lceil 2 \cdot 5 / 3 - 1 \rceil = 3$.
result:
The main theorem, `not_forall_lly_positive_edge_connectivity_threshold_eq_ceil`, refutes the conjectured threshold formula by establishing that it is not the case that $c(n) = \lceil 2n/3 - 1 \rceil$ for all integers $n \ge 3$, where $c(n)$ is the minimum edge-connectivity threshold ensuring everywhere positive Lin–Lu–Yau curvature. In Lean, the theorem `not_forall_lly_positive_edge_connectivity_threshold_eq_ceil` expresses this refutation as the negation of the universal quantification over natural numbers $n : \mathbb{N}$ with $3 \le n$, equating `lly_positive_edge_connectivity_threshold` applied to $n$ with the natural ceiling of $(2n/3) - 1$.

The supporting results formalized alongside the main theorem add the following:

- `lly_positive_edge_connectivity_threshold`: defines the threshold $c(n)$ as the smallest natural number $k$ such that every connected simple graph on $n$ vertices with edge-connectivity at least $k$ has strictly positive Lin–Lu–Yau curvature $\kappa_{\mathrm{LLY}}(x, y) > 0$ on every edge $xy$.
- `lly_curvature_pos_of_edge_connectivity_ge`: proves the upper bound from Theorem 1.3 of arXiv:2610.10559, showing that if a finite connected graph on $n$ vertices has edge-connectivity $\kappa'(G) \ge 2n/3 - 1$, then every edge $xy$ satisfies $\kappa_{\mathrm{LLY}}(x, y) > 0$.
- `lly_positive_edge_connectivity_threshold_three`: computes $c(3) = 0$, showing that every connected graph on 3 vertices has positive Lin–Lu–Yau curvature on every edge regardless of edge-connectivity.
- `lly_positive_edge_connectivity_threshold_five`: establishes that $c(5) = 2$, showing that every connected graph on 5 vertices with edge-connectivity at least 2 has positive Lin–Lu–Yau curvature on every edge, while the tree on 5 vertices with degree sequence containing a vertex of degree 3 (edges $01, 03, 04, 12$) has edge-connectivity 1 and $\kappa_{\mathrm{LLY}}(0, 1) = -1/3$.
proof:
The proof of `not_forall_lly_positive_edge_connectivity_threshold_eq_ceil` proceeds by contradiction using $n = 3$ as an explicit counterexample.

Assume for contradiction that the formula holds universally: for every natural number $n \ge 3$, $c(n) = \lceil 2n/3 - 1 \rceil$. Specializing this universal hypothesis to $n = 3$, using the reflexivity of inequality to discharge the condition $3 \le 3$, yields:
$$ c(3) = \left\lceil \frac{2 \cdot 3}{3} - 1 \right\rceil. $$

Next, rewriting with `lly_positive_edge_connectivity_threshold_three` substitutes the known value $c(3) = 0$. This substitution reduces the equality to:
$$ 0 = \left\lceil \frac{2 \cdot 3}{3} - 1 \right\rceil. $$

Finally, numerical computation evaluates the right-hand side: the expression $(2 \cdot 3)/3 - 1$ simplifies to $1$, whose integer ceiling is $1$. The equality therefore reduces to $0 = 1$, which is a contradiction. This completes the proof.
